essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
Can discourse actually work? Well sure, but also it depends. What are we talking about?  And do we understand each other enough to be able to do that?

A thread🧵 https://t.co/YfdXZfRfjg
Images:

The chart is divided into four quadrants, each representing a different combination of two variables: "How important to my identity is this?" and "How well do I know the person I'm talking to?".

*   The x-axis represents "How well do I know the person I'm talking to?", ranging from "not at all" on the left to "extremely well" on the right.
*   The y-axis represents "How important to my identity is this?", ranging from "not at all" at the bottom to "extremely" at the top.
*   The four quadrants are colored differently:
*   Top-left quadrant: pink, labeled "We're probably gonna fight" with crossed swords emojis.
*   Top-right quadrant: yellow, labeled "We can do this" with heart emojis.
*   Bottom-left quadrant: light green, labeled "Let's get to know each other!" with flexed bicep emojis.
*   Bottom-right quadrant: dark green, labeled "Let's play!" with party popper emojis.

The chart suggests that the outcome of a conversation or interaction depends on the level of familiarity with the other person and the importance of the topic to one's identity. The quadrants provide a humorous and relatable way to understand the potential outcomes of different conversations.

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: HoeMath's Gender Communication Thread: The signifier/signified distinction applied to male/female miscommunication at scale
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
Most women are not (and never will be) capable of telling the truth, because they simply have not grown up enough to stop viewing "the truth" as "what I meant when I said the words."

You say "are you hungry?" And she says "no." You go get food for you and not for her. She is angry. "Why didn't you get me anything?"

"Because you said you weren't hungry."

"But I WAS hungry! I just didn't want to make you feel like you had to get me anything! But I wanted you to!" (So therefore, I did tell the truth.)

This also translates to politics. "I want to live in a diverse country" often means "I don't want to be mean to people by saying I don't." Then they go vote for what they don't want, hoping that they'll get what they do want. Then they don't get it, and it's your fault.

Furthermore, they don't know that you're not doing this.

"I'm not hungry" means "Of course I'm hungry, you should always get me food." You're supposed to know that, because you should imagine being her. Would you be hungry? Yes you would.

So when she says "no," it means "I don't want to be in charge of you getting me food, but you better know I want it and bring some."

Then, when you don't, you OBVIOUSLY knew she wanted food and chose to not get her any. Because you would have been hungry if you were her. So now she's mad.

It is much, much, much easier for men to understand how women communicate than the opposite. For a man to understand a woman, ADD EMOTION. For a woman to understand a man, you have to SUBTRACT EMOTION. This does not compute with women. "Take away all of the feelings from the words and listen to the words."

"But... I still HAVE feelings."

"Right, don't listen to them."

"But I feel like you should know what I feel."

With a large percentage of women, you're not getting anywhere with that. But as a man, you can learn to stop and think: "what would she be feeling when she says this?" Usually, it's as easy as: "what would I be feeling?"

Try it! Next time you're talking with a woman, imagine what she'd be feeling with each message she sends. Then, when you find one that doesn't match what she said, follow the feeling. If you get it right, you might just understand why they vote for all this ridiculous shit.
